claims.title: Proper-partition and Huffman decomposition of prior-weighted zero-error coding
claims.scope: one finite confusion graph, one exact rational source prior, one common deterministic zero-error message, and one binary prefix code
assumptions: every declared source state must be assigned to one independent message class
the receiver knows the codebook and uses prefix framing rather than a separate message-length side channel
expected length is computed under the declared rational source prior
nonclaims: the result does not cover externally framed non-prefix strings, interaction, or block coding
a source prior is a declared model input rather than a representation-independent fact about reality

claims.title: Exact bounded minimum expected prefix code over all proper color partitions
claims.scope: a finite confusion graph below the declared vertex and partition-enumeration caps
assumptions: restricted-growth enumeration visits every unlabeled independent-set partition exactly once
Huffman coding is solved exactly for every enumerated class-probability vector
a cap exceedance raises instead of returning a partial optimum
nonclaims: the exponential bounded algorithm is not a polynomial-time scalability claim
the average-optimal partition is not assumed to use the chromatic number of messages

claims.title: Minimum-coloring-entropy sandwich for exact expected prefix length
claims.scope: the exact finite prior-weighted zero-error prefix-code problem on a nonempty confusion graph
assumptions: Shannon entropy is computed on the message-class distribution induced by a proper partition
binary prefix codes obey Kraft's inequality
the entropy-minimizing and expected-length-minimizing partitions are optimized separately
nonclaims: minimum coloring entropy is not asserted to be the exact one-shot expected prefix length
the one-bit redundancy bound is not an asymptotic graph-power result

claims.title: Fixed-length upper bound with separate mean and peak prefix costs
claims.scope: one finite confusion graph under a declared rational prior and one-shot binary prefix coding
assumptions: a chi-coloring can be represented by ceil(log2 chi) fixed bits
expected and maximum prefix lengths are treated as distinct resources
nonclaims: an expected-length gain does not by itself lower a hard one-shot network cut or deadline
buffering, framing, queueing, and source-process assumptions remain separate

claims.title: Prior-weighted coding monotonicity under confusion-edge deletion
claims.scope: two finite confusion graphs with the same ordered vertices and one graph obtained by deleting edges from the other under the same source prior
assumptions: the communication, prefix-framing, and zero-error conventions are unchanged
every proper partition of the original graph remains feasible after edge deletion
nonclaims: removing an edge need not strictly reduce expected length or chromatic number
more informative side information is an explicit causal resource rather than a free operation

claims.title: Positive-support zero-error coding equals coding the induced support graph
claims.scope: one finite confusion graph with an exact rational prior that may assign zero mass to some declared states
assumptions: support-only zero error quantifies only over states with strictly positive prior mass
declared-state zero error quantifies over every graph vertex regardless of prior mass
nonclaims: rounding a small estimated probability to zero is not a harmless numerical operation under support-only semantics
support-only correctness is not the same guarantee as correctness on every declared state

claims.title: Exact rational ordering of coloring entropies
claims.scope: finite rational probability vectors whose denominators are cleared by one positive integer D
assumptions: zero-mass entropy terms use the convention zero log zero equals zero
probability vectors are compared under the same logarithm base
nonclaims: the displayed decimal entropy is not used to determine the exact minimizing partition
this ordering device does not make irrational empirical probabilities exact

claims.title: Expected-optimal code can use more messages than the chromatic number
claims.scope: the declared five-vertex graph with edges 01,02,03,04,12,23,34 and prior weights (12,19,1,5,13)/50
assumptions: zero error is required for all five states
binary prefix expected length is the optimization objective
all proper partitions below the finite cap are exhausted
nonclaims: using additional colors is not always beneficial
the example does not replace chromatic number for worst-case message-alphabet optimization

claims.title: Skew K4 separates expected, fixed, and peak lengths
claims.scope: the complete four-vertex confusion graph with source prior (7/10,1/10,1/10,1/10)
assumptions: all four states remain zero-error distinguishable
the expected objective uses a binary prefix code under the declared prior
nonclaims: three-bit peak codewords do not fit a two-bit hard cut without buffering or a changed protocol
the source prior is not claimed stationary or known in an empirical deployment

claims.title: Bounded exact prior-weighted graph and prefix-code audit
claims.scope: bounded finite graphs and rational priors, including every labeled four-vertex simple graph
assumptions: direct tests enumerate every deterministic coloring modulo label renaming
small prefix-code optima are independently checked by Kraft-feasible length enumeration
all configured search caps complete without truncation
nonclaims: agreement on bounded graphs is not a large-instance runtime guarantee
a rejected cap is not an optimum, impossibility, or universal theorem receipt
